ctx.x: The two people to deliver it. Ain't any two people that could deliver it as the two people who did it. Just like you Moran and Mack, Amos 'n Andy, two people. One person can't do what two people do. Intonation is one thing, characterization is another, you know. That's what makes gags. Like I tell the gag to my partner and say, "Man why don't you pull your window shades down. I saw you kissing your wife." And the characterization of that is how you laugh. "Whatcha laughing about, I wasn't even home last night."…

I told you about the mule with the light when I was working for the government. I had to strike a match to find my mule at 3 o'clock in the morning. I told you about that. And I told you about how the cart would pick up dirt and I got dumped on the dirt with a truck and all. And I told you about leaving there and going back to Louisville and I used to imagine all these years going and I ain't found a sweetheart. All these years gone by and I haven't found a sweetheart. I go back to school, you know, when I went…

Oh, then I did this what's the name, in Louisville, I worked for what they call the Midtown Grocery Store. I used to deliver groceries from that grocery store. I'd drive a horse and wagon and my father used to work in Louisville Trust Company, firing boilers. He was an engineer-like, huh. That's in Louisville. And in Nashville when my father got the job there when I was going to school there before we were transferred to the 24th School in Indianapolis, my father worked for the Nashville Saddlery Company, you…
